title: Forecast lead time and the timing of crew deployment for weather-driven power outages using AI weather models
abstract: arXiv:2610.20918v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Utilities request mutual aid crews to restore power after severe storms, and requesting early secures more crews but relies on less accurate forecasts. We examined how forecast lead time affects the value of outage predictions for crew deployment, using operational forecasts from two AI weather models, GraphCast and FourCastNet, to predict outage occurrence for counties across the contiguous United States 24 to 120 hours ahead. Forecasts were evaluated by the share of outage burden captured by the counties where crews would be staged. Captured burden declined with lead time: the loss between three and five days was significant in all analyses, whereas the loss within three days was significant only for outages that had not yet started. Early deployment with all requested crews outperformed late deployment with fewer, and we report the availability ratio at which the two break even. translated_title: 使用AI气象模型研究天气驱动停电的预报提前期与抢修队伍部署时机
translated_abstract: 电力公司在严重风暴后会请求互助抢修队伍来恢复供电，尽早请求可以确保获得更多队伍，但依赖于准确度较低的预报。我们研究了预报提前期如何影响停电预测在队伍部署中的价值，利用两个AI气象模型（GraphCast和FourCastNet）的运行预报，预测美国本土各县未来24至120小时的停电发生情况。预报通过队伍驻扎县所捕获的停电负担比例来评估。捕获的负担随提前期增加而下降：三至五天之间的损失在所有分析中均显著，而三天以内的损失仅对尚未开始的停电显著。携带全部请求队伍的早期部署优于携带较少队伍的延迟部署，并报告了两者达到盈亏平衡的可用率。在预报时刻计算的前期地表预测因子……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究利用GraphCast和FourCastNet两个AI气象模型预测美国本土各县未来24至120小时的停电情况，发现尽管预报提前期越长预测价值越低，但尽早部署全部请求的互助抢修队伍总体上优于等待更准确预报后再部署较少队伍的策略。
